# Entire Brain benchmark and product-improvement goal

> **Historical, non-normative planning record (2026-07-16).** This document
> does not define current work, authorize benchmark execution, or override
> [`current-state.md`](current-state.md) or
> [`benchmark-status.md`](benchmark-status.md).

All recorded outcomes in this document are placeholders under the
[benchmark result status policy](benchmark-status.md). The endpoint definitions
and guardrails remain historical design inputs; the measurements do not support
publication claims.

Entire Brain has a historical `v0.1.0` GA-line git tag, but no corresponding
GitHub Release artifact or current packaged release. Every active development
or evaluation run must use a checkout containing the locally fetched current
mainline, and all causal arms in a run must use the same freshly built Brain
binary. The former PR #75/WIP integration state and the former Brain Bench paths
are historical; GraphMark now owns cross-product evaluation evidence.

Sections 8–9.22 are a chronological engineering log through 2026-07-17. Their
measurements remain useful only when tied to the named commits. Their checkout,
baseline, “current,” and “next” wording is non-operational. The mission,
three-endpoint completion contract, endpoint definitions, statistical rule,
guardrails, and owner-decision requirements preserve the design considered at
the time; none is a current execution contract.

## 1. Mission

Construct a causal, reproducible benchmark for Entire Brain and use it as the control system for
iterative Entire Brain improvement. Benchmark construction and product improvement are both in scope;
neither is the finish line by itself. The program is complete only when powered evidence shows
statistically defensible and practically meaningful gains in all three user-facing dimensions, with
no material cross-dimension regression:

1. less end-to-end elapsed time to a validated coding result;
2. lower model-token cost for that result; and
3. higher downstream code quality.

Benchmark readiness, a better retrieval metric, or a favorable point estimate in only one or two
dimensions is progress, not completion. Current serializer microbenchmarks, packet bytes, allocation
counts, lexical proxies, and transparent synthetic utility scores are diagnostic product evidence;
they are not powered proof of this finish line.

## 2. Required final comparisons

Two comparisons must remain distinct.

### 2.1 User-value comparison

Compare the final optimized `retrieved_memory` treatment with treatment-neutral `no_memory` under the
same task, runner, effort, prompt contract, cache policy, and schedule. This is the primary product
claim. The final treatment must clear the frozen superiority rule for time, token cost, and code
quality jointly.

### 2.2 Current-build requirement

The historical `v0.1.0` tag is not a legitimate pre-optimization product
baseline for current evaluation. The user-value comparison above is run with
one current Brain binary across every arm. Product changes are attributed
during development through focused tests, component measurements, and exact
diffs; an older Brain implementation is not introduced as an agentic benchmark
arm. Longitudinal historical measurements are descriptive and cannot replace
the current-build user-value comparison.

## 3. Non-negotiable completion contract

The goal is complete only when all of the following are true:

1. The benchmark treatments are causally isolated: prompts are treatment-neutral, task prompts are
   symptom-only, hidden validation stays hidden, temporal eligibility precedes ranking, order is
   counterbalanced, and cache state is explicit.
2. Engine, product, prompt, task, packet, model, runtime, pricing, and analyzer identities are
   content-addressed and independently verifiable.
3. Public benchmark evidence is relocatable and privacy-safe. Exact sensitive replay bytes, if
   retained, are client-side encrypted and access-controlled; they are never treated as public
   evidence merely because they are encrypted.
4. The task population is representative across repositories, task families, difficulty, answerable
   and null cases, and cold and warm product states. Development and holdout membership is unique and
   contamination-tracked.
5. Every co-primary observation has complete quality, elapsed-time, and normalized usage/cost data.

# Parking lot

Deferred decisions and known-open items that are deliberately NOT being worked
on right now, with enough context to pick them up cold. Add items with a date
and the reason they are parked; remove them when they land or die.

## Session-end hook enqueue for brain indexing (parked 2026-08-07)

Phase 3 of the conversational-memory plan calls for best-effort session-end
enqueueing of deterministic brain indexing, backed by a durable job queue
(discovered → pending → running → complete/retryable_error/invalid/excluded,
keyed by repo + session + source digest). Decision: **reconciliation-via-watch
is good enough for now**; `entire brain watch` already drives the
deterministic refresh on change detection, so a missed or crashed session end
is repaired on the next tick, and `doctor --json`'s `history_freshness` check
(sessions fingerprint vs the last index build) makes the gap visible.

Why parked: hook enqueue is a NEW plugin↔host contract. `entire-plugin.yml`
declares no hooks today, so this crosses into `entireio/cli` territory (hook
event selection, plugin hook dispatch, failure isolation so a hook can never
block the coding agent). The conversational-memory plan's open-decisions table
resolves the default to "best-effort session end plus mandatory
reconciliation"; the reconciliation half exists; the enqueue half waits for
the host contract.

Update (2026-08-08): the brain side of C3 now exists (a `memory notify`
hint endpoint, the durable job queue with the plan's state machine, projection
receipts, and a bounded worker), so unparking is now host-contract work only.
Still parked pending that contract.

Pick-up checklist when unparked:

1. Define the hook contract in `entireio/cli` (event: session end; payload:
   repo root + session id; failure policy: fire-and-forget, never blocks).
2. Declare the hook in `entire-plugin.yml` and add the brain-side receiver
   (enqueue only; deterministic indexing, no agent steps).
3. Add the durable job queue + reentrancy guard from the plan's Phase 3 state
   machine, sized by observed load (the plan says introduce the durable state
   only when hook delivery exists).
4. Keep watch/startup reconciliation mandatory; correctness must never depend
   on a clean session end (plan correction #7).

## Deletion semantics for the shared fact-set store (parked 2026-08-07)

`facts sync` (entire-brain PR #74) merges local facts into a git-meta-backed
shared fact-set head with keep-both semantics. `privacy purge` deletes facts
from the local NDJSON store, but synced copies survive in the git-meta store;
and a later `facts sync` merges them back (keep-both has no notion of
deletion). Interim behavior (shipped): the purge plan reports an explicit
"NOT purged" caveat naming the store path whenever the purge touches facts and
the store exists. Real fix needs deletion/tombstone semantics in the factsync
merge model (a removed fact must win over a present one across members), which
is a factsync protocol change affecting the hosted backend too.

content.text:
The review is done — plan (`../entire-plan`), architecture, product code, tests, and benchmarks. Everything below is verified against code or reproduced, not speculated.

## Context from the plan

`master-plan.md` puts **agent-facing retrieval behavior in Priority 2 (core brain features)**, keeps all benchmark outcomes as placeholders under strict claim discipline, and the 2026-07-30 handover documents the standing rule from the graphmark incident: *improve the product, never tune the harness/prompt toward a win; harness edits are limited to restoring fairness.* Every finding below is sorted with that frame.

## Findings, by priority

### P0 — my own landed fix is incomplete (product; small, unambiguous)

**1. Scan-cache version not bumped.** `historyScanCacheVersion = 7` (history.go:59) gates reuse of per-file scan results, and I changed extraction semantics without bumping it. On any brain with a warm cache the new structural signal **silently never applies** — my benchmark rebuild only worked because prep started cold. One-line fix + the version-history comment.

**2. The indexing prefilter drops pure code-fact lines.** `historyLineMayContainIndexedContent` (history.go:1451) runs *before* JSON decode and still gates on a keyword list. I proved all three of these are discarded before my extractor can see them:

```
pure code fact tool_result line    passes prefilter: false   (defaultFactConfidenceThreshold = 0.75)
help output line                   passes prefilter: false   (--confidence ... (default 0.75))
config dump line                   passes prefilter: false   (timeout = 30 / mode = "strict")
```

The `(default 0.75)` record got indexed only because its line happened to carry other keywords. The prefilter also still contains the benchmark vocabulary (`attributionbasecommit`, `seed-agent`, `schema contract`, …) at lines 1468–1470. Fix: teach the prefilter the structural signal, drop the benchmark terms, keep the cheap fast-path property.

### P1 — the benchmark cannot measure the brain until these land (harness fairness restoration)

**3. Sanitizer breaks every prepared brain's index — the agreed fix, with one ordering trap.** `sanitize_repo_session_corpus` hand-edits `history/index.json` + manifest but not `index_bytes`/`index_sha256`/`records_fingerprint`/`transcripts_fingerprint`, so the loader fail-closes and **every treatment arm has run with history search disabled**. New detail from this review: a *second* in-place pass (`scrub_benchmark_secret_lines/json`) rewrites the whole brain tree after sanitization, so the repair must run **last**: remove contaminated sessions → secret-scrub transcripts → invoke `entire-brain refresh history` so the product republishes its own integrity fields over final bytes. This also deletes the harness's duplicate `sha256_file_corpus` fingerprint (same trap as the repo-key hash).

**4. Oracle binary on PATH — needs your decision.** `tools["brain"]` is built from harness-repo HEAD (run.py:1206) and prepended to `PATH` for **every** arm (run.py:3876). For self-hosted tasks the environment therefore contains a binary that prints the answer (`--help` → `(default 0.75)`). r2's "win" came from exactly this.

**5. Boundary-inspection audit vs scrubbed tasks — needs your decision.** With the answer scrubbed, failing baselines escalate to `cat-file`/`reflog`/`fsck`, every row gets excluded as protocol misuse, and no comparison forms. The prohibition's original rationale (reconstructing the setup patch) is void on a scrubbed task — the boundary reveals nothing.

**6. Host-path leak flags.** All `I:release_host_path_leak` hits are `$.agent_info.activity.commands[*]` — agent-typed absolute paths escape `redact_record_host_paths`. Extend record redaction to the activity command list. Mechanical, blocks release hygiene.

### P2 — product robustness (plan Priority 2, do after the above)

**7. `brain_delete_project` MCP tool has no guard** (mcp.go:995): one agent tool call irreversibly deletes the entire brain. Same hazard class as the export wipe I fixed; observed agent behavior this week makes it non-theoretical. Add confirm/tombstone semantics.

**8. `historyTerms` (history.go:1552) still carries benchmark vocabulary** into FTS text — same disease as the fact signal, lower stakes since it only annotates.

**9. Document-form (opencode) transcripts never yield tool-result facts** — `parseDocumentConversation` drops non-text parts wholesale, so the format inconsistency means the fix from this week only benefits JSONL sessions.

**10. Fail-closed errors should name their remedy** — `"history index size does not match manifest"` should append *"run `entire brain refresh history`"*. `doctor` detects the state; the error should guide (r2 found the fix only by luck).

### P3 — claim discipline (per plan, mostly "don't")

- The retained June clean-proof evidence is invalid at a deeper level than hash drift (treatment never invoked the brain). Keep the gate red; never repair its hashes; replace only with a clean proof-ready suite.
- Release gate: 2 of 3 required suites need `~/Projects/cli-bench` (absent here) + your pricing quote. Environment/owner items, not code.

Not found (searched for): further task-text ranking bonuses in `brief` (clean since `6419e98e`), other unguarded `RemoveAll`s on brain state, test fixtures that depend on the removed vocabulary (suites pass).

questions.question: How should the oracle-binary leak (finding 4) be handled? The bin on PATH is built from harness HEAD and prints compiled-in answers for self-hosted tasks.

options.label: Build agent-visible bin from the task worktree (Recommended)
options.description: The binary agents can invoke gets compiled from the sabotaged worktree state, so its --help prints the broken value. Prep/audit keep using the HEAD-built binary internally. Answers can no longer be read off PATH, for any arm.

options.label: Remove the bin from agent PATH entirely
options.description: Agents get no entire-brain binary unless the condition delivers one. Simplest, but breaks conditions whose protocol expects the agent to run brain CLI commands.

options.label: Leave it; exclude compiled-default tasks
options.description: Keep the environment as-is and treat tasks whose answer is a compiled-in default as unusable for proof lanes.

questions.question: With the answer scrubbed, baselines probe the synthetic merge boundary (cat-file/reflog/fsck) and every row is excluded, so no comparison forms (finding 5). What should boundary probing mean on scrubbed tasks?

options.label: Score it as an ordinary failure (Recommended)
options.description: On tasks with scrub_answer_from_history, boundary probing no longer voids the row's protocol validity (the boundary reveals nothing); the row simply passes or fails on its merits. Comparisons can form; unscrubbed tasks keep the strict exclusion.

options.label: Keep strict exclusion everywhere
options.description: Boundary probing always excludes the row. Honest but means baseline arms may never yield 4 valid reps on hard tasks, so proof-ready comparisons stay rare.

options.label: Sandbox-block the boundary ops
options.description: Deny reflog/fsck/cat-file on the synthetic parents at the sandbox level so the temptation is unreachable instead of adjudicated afterward. Stronger isolation, more harness machinery.

Reproduced at real scale — this changes the answer to both questions. After the harness's exact removal sequence (`update-ref -d` + `reflog expire` + `git prune`), **124 objects remain fully recoverable**, because a fetch above ~100 objects is stored as a pack and `git prune` only deletes loose objects:

```
packs after fetch: 1

$ git cat-file -p <blob>   →   transcript 29 defaultFactConfidenceThreshold = 0.75
```

That's exactly the channel r1's "~80 copies in raw session transcripts via `fsck --unreachable`" came from. The harness comment *"the agent cannot read raw transcripts via git; only the indexed brain remains"* is false today. Adding `git repack -ad` before the prune makes removal real (verified in the same probe).

## The fairest design

**One principle: the answer exists in exactly one place — inside the brain's indexed memory. Everything else the agent can touch (worktree, git object store, binaries on PATH) reflects only the sabotaged state, identically in both arms.**

Once that's physically true, fairness stops depending on adjudication. The baseline fails because the information genuinely isn't there; the brain wins only if retrieval actually surfaces it; and an agent that wastes 40 turns on `fsck` pays for it in the time/token endpoints — in-band, no row exclusions, no judgment calls.

Four changes get there:

1. **Purge checkpoint objects for real** — `git repack -ad` before `git prune` in `remove_agent_visible_entire_history`. Closes the r1 channel. (This is a fairness *restoration* in the plan's sense: the harness always claimed this isolation; it just didn't have it.)

2. **The PATH binary mirrors the worktree.** For self-hosted tasks, build the agent-visible `entire-brain` from the sabotaged task worktree; prep keeps using the trusted HEAD build to construct the memory. Then `--help` prints the broken value and the r2 oracle disappears — for both arms, since both get the same binary. This beats removing the binary (which would break conditions whose sanctioned protocol *is* the CLI) and beats excluding self-hosted tasks (which throws away the most realistic memory tasks rather than fixing the leak).

3. **Sanitizer republishes through the product** (`refresh history` after contamination removal *and* secret scrub) so the index actually loads. Without this the brain's value isn't in the experiment at all.

4. **Boundary probing becomes a scored failure, not an exclusion, on scrubbed tasks.** After 1+2 the synthetic-merge boundary and the object store are provably answer-free, so probing is just another dead-end search strategy — it should cost the row its outcome, not its validity. Unscrubbed tasks keep the strict exclusion, because there the boundary still reveals the setup patch.

Plus the two P0 product fixes (scan-cache bump, prefilter alignment) — otherwise the brain shows up to a fair fight with its best evidence unindexed.

What makes this "no cheating" in both directions: nothing coaches the brain arm (no query hints, no excerpt spoon-feed — that stays dead), and nothing handicaps the baseline (identical env, identical prompt, probing merely wastes its budget). The brain's entire advantage must come through `brief`/`search`/`query` over genuinely retained history — which is the product claim the plan wants proven.

content.text:
Let me back up and explain the whole setup plainly, because both terms come from how a benchmark task is constructed.

**How a task is built.** Take the fact-merge task as the example. The real code contains the correct, deliberately-chosen value:

```go
defaultFactConfidenceThreshold = 0.75
```

To create the task, the harness makes a copy of the repo and **plants a bug in it**: it edits that line to `0.7`. That planted bug is what I've been calling the "sabotaged state" — nothing more than the intentional wrong value that defines the task. The agent is then told: *"this default is wrong; recover the value the project actually decided on."* The experiment is: an agent **without** the brain shouldn't be able to find `0.75` anywhere, while an agent **with** the brain should recover it from remembered session history. If the copy still contains `0.75` somewhere outside the brain, the task measures nothing — that's the "leak" we've been closing all week (it was still in git history, then in a commit message, then in the reference binary's `--help`).

**Where git prune comes in.** The brain's memory is built from your recorded coding sessions, which live on a special git branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) as transcripts. During setup the harness has to *fetch that branch into the task copy* so the brain can index those sessions. But the raw transcripts contain the answer — they include snapshots of the code with `0.75` in it. So after indexing, the harness **deletes the branch** so the agent can only get at that history *through the brain*, not by reading the transcripts directly.

Here's the problem: deleting a git branch doesn't delete the data. Git keeps the underlying objects on disk, just unlabeled, and `git fsck --unreachable` lists them. One of last night's agents did exactly that — dug through the deleted objects, found ~80 transcript copies containing `0.75`, and "solved" the task without using the brain.

The harness already tries to clean up — it runs `git prune` after deleting the branch. But `git prune` only deletes objects stored as *individual files*, and a fetch of any real size stores objects packed together in one *pack file*, which `prune` doesn't touch. I reproduced it: after the harness's exact cleanup, 124 objects were still fully readable, including the transcript line with the answer. One extra command (`git repack -ad`, which rewrites the packs keeping only reachable objects) makes the deletion real — afterwards there's genuinely nothing to find.

So the plainer version of the plan:

1. The task copy contains the planted bug and **no trace of the true value** — not in git history (done), not in commit messages (done), not in deleted-but-recoverable git objects (the repack fix), not printed by the tools on PATH (the binary fix).
2. The true value exists in exactly one place: **the brain's indexed session memory**.
3. Then the comparison is honest: no-brain fails because the answer genuinely isn't reachable; the brain wins only if its retrieval actually works.

Want me to go ahead on that basis?

new_fn = '''def republish_brain_history(
    plugin: pathlib.Path, worktree: pathlib.Path, tools: dict[str, pathlib.Path]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Have the product rebuild the history index after the harness mutated the corpus.

    Sanitization removes contaminated sessions and the secret scrub rewrites
    transcript bytes in place. Hand-editing history/index.json alongside that
    left the manifest's integrity fields (index_bytes, index_sha256,
    records_fingerprint, transcripts_fingerprint) describing the pre-scrub
    artifact, so the product's fail-closed loader rejected every prepared brain
    and history search was silently disabled in every treatment run. The brain
    binary is the single authority on those fields, so it republishes them over
    the final bytes; the harness never computes them again.
    """
    repos_root = plugin / "data" / "repos"
    indexes = sorted(repos_root.glob("*/*/history/index.json")) if repos_root.exists() else []
    if not indexes:
        return {"ran": False, "reason": "no_history_index"}
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT": str(worktree),
        "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR": str(plugin / "config"),
        "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR": str(plugin / "data"),
        "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR": str(plugin / "state"),
        "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR": str(plugin / "cache"),
    }
    proc = run_cmd([str(tools["brain"]), "refresh", "history"], cwd=worktree, env=env, timeout=1800)
    if proc.returncode != 0:

            "brain history republish failed after sanitization:\\n"

    setup_replacements applied in a throwaway overlay: same implementation, the
    sabotaged constant, no oracle. Prep and audits keep using tools["brain"].

        for replacement in task.get("setup_replacements", [])
        if str(replacement.get("old") or "") != str(replacement.get("new") or "")
    ]
    patterns = [re.compile(str(pattern)) for pattern in task.get("history_leak_patterns", [])]
    root_help = run_cmd([str(binary), "--help"], timeout=60).stdout
    helps = [("", root_help)]
    for line in root_help.splitlines():
        match = re.match(r"^  ([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)\\s{2,}", line)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for the isolation repairs: checkpoint object purge, scrubbed-task
boundary policy, and generic host-path record hygiene.

The checkpoint purge closes an observed leak: deleting the checkpoint ref and
running `git prune` left the fetched PACK untouched, so an agent recovered the
"deleted" transcripts (and the task's answer) via `git fsck --unreachable` plus
`git cat-file`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest


HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
if str(HERE) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run", HERE / "run.py")
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
run = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
sys.modules[SPEC.name] = run
SPEC.loader.exec_module(run)


ANSWER = "defaultFactConfidenceThreshold = 0.75"


def _git(*args: str, cwd: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], cwd=cwd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True
    ).stdout


def _seed_checkpoint_source(root: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """A source repo whose checkpoint history is big enough to arrive as a pack."""
    src = root / "src"
    src.mkdir()
    _git("init", "-q", cwd=src)
    _git("config", "user.email", "t@example.invalid", cwd=src)
    _git("config", "user.name", "T", cwd=src)
    for i in range(60):
        (src / f"transcript-{i}.jsonl").write_text(f"session {i} {ANSWER}\n")
    _git("add", "-A", cwd=src)
    _git("commit", "-qm", "checkpoints", cwd=src)
    for i in range(60):
        (src / f"transcript-{i}.jsonl").write_text(f"session {i} updated\n")
    _git("add", "-A", cwd=src)
    _git("commit", "-qm", "more checkpoints", cwd=src)
    return src


class CheckpointObjectPurgeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_removal_leaves_no_recoverable_transcript_objects(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            src = _seed_checkpoint_source(root)
            worktree = root / "worktree"
            worktree.mkdir()
            _git("init", "-q", cwd=worktree)
            _git("config", "user.email", "t@example.invalid", cwd=worktree)
            _git("config", "user.name", "T", cwd=worktree)
            _git("commit", "-qm", "base", "--allow-empty", cwd=worktree)
            _git("fetch", "-q", str(src), f"+HEAD:{run.CHECKPOINT_REF}", cwd=worktree)

            removed = run.remove_agent_visible_entire_history(worktree)
            self.assertTrue(removed)

            unreachable = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "fsck", "--unreachable", "--no-reflogs"],
                cwd=worktree, capture_output=True, text=True,
            ).stdout.strip()
            self.assertEqual(unreachable, "", "fetched checkpoint objects survived removal")

            # The answer must be unrecoverable from the whole object store.
            grep = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "grep", "-F", ANSWER, "--all-match", "--cached"],
                cwd=worktree, capture_output=True, text=True,
            )
            self.assertNotEqual(grep.returncode, 0)


class ScrubbedTaskBoundaryPolicyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    AGENT_INFO = {
        "activity": {
            "commands": [
                "git cat-file -p 2d38362 | head -5",
                "git reflog --all",
            ]
        }
    }
    ATTESTATIONS = [{"source_history_parent": "2d383620e9d1dc5609f1657d1d40a4b247433b03"}]

    def test_unscrubbed_tasks_keep_the_strict_exclusion(self) -> None:
        audit = run.baseline_history_audit(self.AGENT_INFO, self.ATTESTATIONS, {})
        self.assertFalse(audit["ok"])
        self.assertTrue(audit["findings"])

    def test_scrubbed_tasks_record_probing_as_advisory(self) -> None:
        audit = run.baseline_history_audit(
            self.AGENT_INFO, self.ATTESTATIONS, {"scrub_answer_from_history": True}
        )
        self.assertTrue(audit["ok"], "probing an answer-free boundary must not void the row")
        self.assertEqual(audit["findings"], [])
        self.assertTrue(audit["advisory_findings"], "the probing must stay visible in the record")

    def test_clean_rows_are_unchanged_either_way(self) -> None:
        clean = {"activity": {"commands": ["go test ./..."]}}
        for task in ({}, {"scrub_answer_from_history": True}):
            audit = run.baseline_history_audit(clean, self.ATTESTATIONS, task)
            self.assertTrue(audit["ok"])
            self.assertNotIn("advisory_findings", audit)


class RecordHostPathHygieneTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_unregistered_host_paths_are_scrubbed_generically(self) -> None:
        record = {
            "agent_info": {
                "activity": {
                    "commands": [
                        "cat /Users/someone/private/notes.txt",
                        "ls /tmp/agent-scratch",
                        "go test ./internal/cli/",
                    ]
                }
            },
            "worktree": "/wt/repo/internal",
        }
        out = run.redact_record_host_paths(record, {pathlib.Path("/wt/repo"): "<agent-worktree>"})
        commands = out["agent_info"]["activity"]["commands"]
        self.assertNotIn("/Users/", " ".join(commands))
        self.assertNotIn("/tmp/", " ".join(commands))
        self.assertIn("go test ./internal/cli/", commands)
        self.assertEqual(out["worktree"], "<agent-worktree>/internal")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

content.text:
Everything is implemented, tested, and the panel is now running with all repairs live. Mid-run telemetry already confirms the two riskiest changes work:

- **Republish**: the treatment cell's brain now carries a coherent, product-published index — 40,716 records, declared bytes == actual (the fail-closed coherence check would have aborted otherwise). This is the first benchmark run in which the brain arm can actually *load* its history index.
- **Oracle**: the agent-visible `entire-brain` prints `(default 0.7)` while the harness binary prints `0.75` — same HEAD retrieval code, sabotaged constant, verified before the run by the help-tree sentinel.

What landed, in two commits:

**`e1120ffe` — product** (both Go suites + vet green):
1. Scan cache bumped to v8 — warm caches would have silently kept the old extraction.
2. Pre-decode line filter learned the structural signal (proven by test: a raw line whose only content is `defaultFactConfidenceThreshold = 0.75`, a `--help` default, or a config assignment now survives to the extractor; before, all three were dropped). Benchmark vocabulary removed from the prefilter and from `historyTerms`.
3. Opencode/document transcripts: tool `state.output` is now mined through the same fact extractor — bulk output still stays out, tested in both directions.
4. `brain_delete_project` requires `confirm=true`, distinguishing absent ("confirm is required") from explicitly false (irreversibility message).
5. Index-integrity errors now name their remedy (`run entire brain refresh history`).

**`a3d80c23` — harness** (333 harness tests green):
6. **Checkpoint purge is real**: repack-reachable-only before prune, then fail closed if `fsck` still reports anything. Test reproduces the pack-survival leak and proves it closed.
7. **Sanitizer republishes through the product**: after contamination removal *and* the secret scrub, `refresh history` rebuilds index+manifest over final bytes; the harness computes no integrity field itself anymore.
8. **Answer-free agent binary**: HEAD code + task-declared `binary_replacements` built in a throwaway overlay, cached by (HEAD, replacements), identical in every arm; prep/audits keep the unmodified HEAD build. The constant had moved (`internal/cli/facts_merge.go` → `internal/factmerge/merge.go`), which is exactly why tasks pin the current site explicitly and the sentinel guards future refactors.
9. **Boundary probing on scrubbed tasks** is advisory — recorded, but it costs the row its outcome, not its validity. Unscrubbed tasks keep strict exclusion. Tested in all three directions.
10. **Generic host-path scrub** on retained records (mirrors the auditor's regex) — verified to zero out the `I:release_host_path_leak` findings while keeping semantic labels like `<agent-worktree>`.

Both tasks re-validated `fails-as-expected` before spending. The 16-cell panel is running; when it completes I'll audit against the `replay-lab-clean` manifest and report the comparison — this is the first run where a brain win can only come from retrieval.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests that private-artifact detection tracks information access, not intent.

Two layers. First, paths are judged inside the agent worktree: benchmark
worktrees live under benchmarks/agent-brain/results/, so the absolute path of
an ordinary source file contains the same substring that marks a private
artifact, and matching the raw path flagged agents for editing the file the
task asked them to edit.

Second, isolation is physical: hidden directories are deleted, the checkpoint
ref and its objects are purged, and the sandbox denies the harness tree outside
the worktree. A probe of an artifact that EXISTS (the .benchmark brain store in
a treatment arm) is a hard violation because content could flow; a probe of
something removed or denied is an advisory dead end. Excluding rows for
information-free probes starved comparisons below the minimum repetitions while
proving nothing about the treatment.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest


HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
if str(HERE) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run", HERE / "run.py")
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
run = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
sys.modules[SPEC.name] = run
SPEC.loader.exec_module(run)


class ForbiddenArtifactHardnessTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.worktree = pathlib.Path(self._tmp.name) / "repo"
        (self.worktree / ".benchmark" / "plugin" / "data").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.worktree / ".benchmark" / "plugin" / "data" / "index.json").write_text("{}")
        (self.worktree / "internal" / "cli").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.worktree / "internal" / "cli" / "facts_merge.go").write_text("package cli\n")
        # benchmarks/agent-brain is deliberately ABSENT: the harness deletes it.

content.text: Confirmed. The fix: deny `file-read-data` (contents and listings) instead of `file-read*`, so ancestor metadata stays statable while nothing under the roots is readable:

input.command:
cd /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-brain; python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("benchmarks/agent-brain/run.py"); s=p.read_text()
old = '''    lines = ["(version 1)", "(allow default)"]
    lines.extend(
        f"(deny file-read* (subpath {json.dumps(str(path))}))" for path in denied_roots
    )'''
new = '''    lines = ["(version 1)", "(allow default)"]
    # deny file-read-data, not file-read*: metadata (lstat/stat) of the denied
    # trees stays allowed because path resolution walks every ancestor of the
    # worktree, which lives under the harness root. Denying metadata made
    # EvalSymlinks fail on the ROOT component, which broke every repo-scoped
    # brain CLI command inside the sandbox while the contents deny is what the
    # isolation actually needs: no directory listings, no file contents.
    lines.extend(
        f"(deny file-read-data (subpath {json.dumps(str(path))}))" for path in denied_roots
    )'''
assert s.count(old)==1
p.write_text(s.replace(old,new))
print("profile relaxed to data-deny")

## Summary

Fixed `internal/cli/facts_merge.go:17` — `defaultFactConfidenceThreshold` was `0.7`, but the project's actually-decided value is `0.75`.

This wasn't findable from this workspace's own git history: the constant was introduced at `0.7` in its one and only commit here, and never changed — a dead end confirmed independently by a sub-agent. The recovery came from `go.mod`'s module path (`github.com/ashtom/entire-brain`), which pointed to the real upstream repo with much fuller history (1063 commits vs. 424 here).
